title: Mate in Two
concept: Check, then check again. Forcing moves leave no time to escape.

glossary.definition: A check, a capture or a threat that your opponent has to answer right away.

summary: For mate in two, start with forcing moves: checks first, then captures. After each one, picture the king's escape squares, and find the move that takes the last one away.

narration: Black's bishop grabs a piece on c4. Black has more material, so you'd better find something forcing.
Rook to f8, check! The only way to stop it is to block with the bishop on g8.
Bishop to g8. Now look at Black's king: g8, g7 and h7 are all filled by Black's own pieces.
Knight to f7, smothered mate! The king is buried by its own army, and the knight jumps in for the kill.

guided.hint: Black's king is out in the open on h8. Which queen check comes with a follow-up?
guided.explanation: Queen to h5, check along the h-file. The king's only move is g8, and then queen to h7 is checkmate: your pawn on g6 guards her, so the king can't take.

guided.hint: White's king is stuck behind its own pawns. Check it on the back row, and see what White can use to block.
guided.explanation: Rook to c1, check! White's only block is the rook on d1, but nothing protects it there. You take it, and it's back-rank mate.

guided.hint: Your knight on h5 is in your queen's way on the h-file. Can it move out of the way with check?
guided.explanation: Knight to f6, check! It clears the h-file for your queen, and Black has to take it. Now queen to h7 is checkmate: the knight on g5 protects her. A sacrifice that clears the way is called a clearance.
